Methods
The study consisted of two phases of weekly social media posts. In
each phase, 15 posts were published on the same day and time, while
engagement was monitored. Three different types of posts were
created, that were sequential cycling each week. Type 1 was written
informative content related to research activities; type 2 was image
content related to the research activities and equipment, with a short
text caption of the image; and type 3 was image content with people –
scientists working on research activities with a short text caption of
the image.



Results
Poisson regression analysis revealed that type 3 posts result in the
most audience engagement on LinkedIn, suggesting that using
images of people in combination with short text captions is the most
effective way to engage social media audiences. These findings can

no significant difference between the two phases in relation to

Furthermore, we identified limitations of our study. First, the
audience in this study is related to one institution (research
organization). Accordingly, the audience may have its own
characteristics which are not representative of the larger population. With available analytical tools the audience was studied
on each social media channels, however these functions are limited and not all social media channels offer the same kind of
data, which is another limitation. Comparability of the three
social media channels is an additional limitation. The number of
followers is different on the three channels and there might be
an overlap between followers. However, in the analysis we
did account for repeated measures of the same post on different platform by including the unique post ID as a source
of random error. While it is likely there is some duplication

The structural characteristics of the 'networks' of the InnoRenew CoE on these three different channels, have been provided at the beginning of the Materials and methods section. This demographic data has not been used to evaluate the 'measures of engagement' on this different platforms.

The research idea is innovative, and I appreciate how the authors are trying to do the
operationalization with some acknowledged limits. My suggestion is to have different sections
between Introduction and Theoretical Background (Literature Review). The current introduction
section reads more like a theoretical background. I would suggest having an introduction that
gives a non-technical audience a general overview of the topic. This is important as the authors
are trying to do interdisciplinary research (e.g., communication, social media, sustainability, and
construction).
I am also curious about how the authors address research questions. In my opinion, the research
questions resemble specific and testable hypotheses. If my guess is right, with the same spirit of
reaching a non-technical audience, I would suggest breaking down the theoretical background
per hypothesis.
Kudos for your hard work.

There is very little engagement with the literature. This is at the beginning of the paper and is
mainly concerned about communciation. However, the realities of scientific communication
through social media have not been explored.
The structural characteristics of the 'networks' of the InnoRenew CoE on these three different
channels, have been provided at the beginning of the Materials and methods section. This
demographic data has not been used to evaluate the 'measures of engagement' on this different
platforms.

The discussion is mainly based on the number of impressions, shares and comments. The
differences between these 'measures of engagement' by different users has not been established
in enough depth. For example, there is a claim that "users may not be comfortable commenting
on topics connected to sustainable construction, or that they are not interested in engaging in
conversations on social media to develop new relationships." As far as the paper is concerned, this
correlation is now based on any evidence.
